## Part A - Creating Vectors and List:

##Question #1:
##a. Create a vector for the worker’s age.
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
```
##b. How many data points?
```{r}
length(age)
```
##c. Find minimum and the maximum value of worker's age.
```{r}
min(age)
max(age)
```
##d.Accesss the 13rd to the 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of the worker's Age.
```{r}
age[c(13:18,33:35)]
```
##e. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th, and 40th elements are not included.
```{r}
age[-c(10,20,30,40)]
```
##f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th and 44th elements with value=0.
```{r}
age[c(14,24,34,44)] <- 0
```
##Question #2
```{r}
data(rivers)
```
##a. 
```{r}
length(rivers)
sum(rivers)
mean(rivers)
median(rivers)
var(rivers)
sd(rivers)
min(rivers)
max(rivers)
```
##b.
```{r}
river_summary <- c(length=length(rivers), sum=sum(rivers), mean=mean(rivers), median=median(rivers), variance=var(rivers), standard_deviation=sd(rivers),minimum=min(rivers),maximum=max(rivers))

```

#Forbes Ranking
##a. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling. Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90.
```{r}
power_ranking[19] <-15
pay[19] <-90
```

```{r}
vegetables <- c("Carrots", "Potato", "Cabbage", "Garlic", "Tomato", "Ginger", "Onion", "String Beans", "Pumpkin", "Cucumber")
vegetables
```
